claims.claim: The keyboard and mouse controls are described as difficult or nearly impossible to use with the default bindings.

citations.review_text:
I played through the base game on Switch when it came out, and recently bought it on sale here with the Sunbreak expansion. I have played MonHun since 4U. If you want to play MonHun on steam but DON'T want to pay the price of Wilds, Rise is a great alternative.

Pros:
+You can zoom around the map like your friendly neighborhood Spiderman.
+QoL improvements (no hot/cold drinks needed), but still offers enough challenge.
+My computer used to crash a lot in World and had long loading screens in World. I hear similar issues exist in Wilds. I do not have these issues in Rise.
+Great new monsters, fun returning monsters, interesting maps.
+All weapons are viable. This is unlike MH4 where Insect Glaive dominated the meta.
+The girl who gives you quests is very cute.

Cons:
-Strictly speaking, World is probably the better game.
-Way too many tutorials in the start of the game.
-Rise's player base is split between PC/Steam and Switch. There is no cross-platform play.
-My heart goes out to keyboard/mouse players. You'll be using the F1-12 keys while in combat.
-Almudron exists in this game.

This "PC port" is an absolute insolence. It is basically impossible to play with keyboard / mouse.
The default bindings are LITERALLY impossible to use (unless you have 3 hands) and rebinding is nearly impossible, because it refuses many keys on your keyboard, no combos, and it constantly complains that hotkeys are used twice
The internet / youtube is FULL of people complaining about it. Should have researched better.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Mid-game adventurers praise the strong performance across various systems, while highlighting mandatory defense quests as tedious filler.

claims.claim: Rampage defense quests are described as mandatory for story progression and weapon upgrades while being considered tedious tower defense filler.

citations.review_text: The worst part of the game, the Rampage defense quests, are just FINE. Everything else is fantastic.

As someone who started their MG journey with Freedom on PSP,  Rise is the weakest mainline entry for me by a clear margin. Malzeno was the one fight I enjoyed, everything else felt forgettable.

The wirebug changes traversal in a way I don't particularly love, you're not tracking or finding monsters anymore, you're just zipping straight to a map marker, and a lot of the actual "hunting" feeling gets lost in the process. The base roster also leans hard on returning monsters rather than new fights (something like 40+ monsters out of the 60 are returning ones), which made the campaign feel thinner than it should. And Rampage quests are just bad, tower defense fillers that has nothing to do with why I play these games.

The setting doesn't do it for me either, Kamura's whole feudal-Japan aesthetic is a big departure from the tone the series usually goes for, and it never clicked with me the way past locales did. I just enjoy the vague but unique fantasy they usually go for way more. It's much more creative and unique.

If you're coming from World or earlier and expecting that game to feel like Monster Hunter, temper expectations, Sunbreak fixes a bit of this, but base Rise on its own is the low point of the series for me.

While I like the boss rush element that this installment have, I don't understand why 'rampage' is even in the game. This game mode alone soils my experience for MH Rise since some of them are mandatory for story progression and improving weapons. Dare I say that it is 'clunkier' than MH World. It's very tedious and it felt like a chore.

citations.review_text:
[h1]"Hunt" badass monsters with badass weapons[/h1]

The Monster Hunter series is about hunting monsters... Actually, that's a bit of a lie: Unlike in real life, you don't track the animals, they're shown on the map right away. You also don't get to prod the animals from a safe distance, chasing them, tiring them out and eventually slaying them when they're at their weakest.

Instead, the moment these animals set their eyes on you, their life mission changes from "eat, sleep, breed" to "♥♥♥♥ this one fellow in particular". The game features all kinds of monsters with all kinds of ways to make mince-meat out of you with their fangs, claws, talons and spiked tails. Or burnt meat, electrocuted meat, iced meat... Hell, some of them just yell at you so loud that it kills you.

Fortunately, you are given quite a few methods in killing these monsters. Your main tools will be the weapons, and you can choose between 14 of them. You have simple ones like sword and shield, two swords, one sword the length of your character, and one sword the length [i]and[/i] width of your character. Then you have a lance, and a lance that shoots explosives. An axe that transforms into a sword and explodes. A bow, and a bow shaped like a hip-wielded gun. I hope you aren't missing the cool-factor that I'm painstakingly trying to write into the subtext here.

Each weapon plays quite differently from each other, and they all have a lot of depth to them. Some weapons require some memorization of combos to be able to do some big finisher style move at the end, other weapons need you to counter a monster's moves right before they hit you, and others have you act like an annoying bee, doing simple, small damage attacks while constantly being close to the monster. Each of these weapon types is very much viable to get you through the entire game, you don't need to change for a specific monster if you don't want to. You should try them out, and use what you find the most comfortable. There's no …

[h1]What happened to hunting monsters?[/h1]
My first MH experience was Monster Hunter Tri on the Wii in 2010 with my older brother. I vividly remember watching in awe as he tracked down and fought a Lagiacrus for 30 minutes with a Great Sword, eventually slaying it within the underwater cave of Area 12.
Fast forward to 2022, and I decided to try out MH Rise on my own PC. The first thing I remember was being introduced to some cat for a support, a rideable dog… that can drift and boost like it’s Mario Kart, and an owl that feeds me the live location of every single large monster on the map from the second I spawn into a quest. At this rate, the next major MH title will have drones conducting surveillance sweeps & missile strikes. Once I finished naming these “companions” and learning how to take pictures for some reason, I was finally able to hunt… or so I thought. It was more of an anticlimactic arcade fight. The Avengers & I practically slaughtered a Great Jagg-Izuchi in 5 minutes. The next 100 hours or so weren't much different. Some fights took longer because monsters had more health, but that’s about it. I lost interest when I realized I had yet to actually HUNT a single monster. Half the time, I'm mounted on one monster while attacking another. Makes them feel less like monsters and more like little pets. Don't even get me started on the wirebug. Rise holds BOTH your hands while your personal SEAL Team 6 does half the work for you. It’s just not exhilarating gameplay for me, nor is it rewarding when I’m served everything on a silver platter. If you’re looking for an authentic & challenging Monster Hunter experience, I’d highly recommend an older MH title.

Coming from Monster Hunter World, it’s not necessarily more of the same as the core concepts are different, favouring faster fights, more mobile enemies, smaller maps and a more streamlined experience with a more arcade-like direction. The game is better when you have the Sunbreak DLC, which really opens up the experience and keeps it fresh. 

Pros
Some good changes to existing monsters, with a nice new roster of its own and relatively better hitboxes on new enemies. Wirebugs add some mobility and makes combat more dynamic. Palamutes are a nice addition and are fun to have around and use to explore maps. More customisation of individual skills through wirebug use and builds. World design, characters, NPCs and the soundtracks are great. NPCs are a great addition and probably the best part of Rise, as each character is unique, helpful and specialises in different weapons and aspects of combat. This keeps hunts fresh, allows for better single-player quest experiences and makes these NPCs feel alive. They each get mini quests/hunts to complete and then get recruited. Overall, the game feels cosy with its setting, your character origins and the hub areas, which are each distinct but have character. 

Cons
Maps can feel dead compared to World; most of it is a blur because you are riding on your Palamute to hunts, which are all marked. No more tracking monsters and seeing their habitats and then coming face to face with them, or being ambushed – it’s all marked on the map, taking that sense of exploration and discovery away. Wyvern riding is cool the first few times, but it gets boring, and if using NPCs, it happens all the time, so there is no need for you to engage in the mechanic. Spirit birds are probably the worst mechanic ever, apart from Rampage fights, tedious and bloated for no reason. The grind can be felt, which is not a good thing because then you won’t want to boot the game up to fight the same handful of monsters. Gear and skills changes are questionabl…

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the multiplayer matchmaking lacks a list or search system for join requests, making it difficult to find and join random anomaly quests or specific sessions.

citations.review_text:
Coming from World, I'm definitely enjoying this one way more. Weapons don't feel as impactful as they do in World, which is disappointing at first, however the game makes up for it with its improved moveset which makes the combat way more fun. You also have special moves for each weapon, and you can unlock more as you play and change them to your liking.

The disappointing part is that the game lacks the SOS system from World. You can only create or join lobbies, or search for random or specific mission, not an issue if you play with friends.

It's a big difference coming from Monster Hunter World or Wilds. Combat is way faster and monsters have tons of agility and moves to counter your mobility skills. The switch skill system is amazing, and Sunbreak adds even more to experiment with. Also, this game has the single best iteration of Gunlance in the entire series, based on Blast Dash alone. It's like playing Insect Glaive, except you have a bazooka instead of a stick. Sunbreak is an incredible expansion, and vastly improves on the shortcomings of the base game. Monster variety is great too. The endgame is super expansive, but the anomaly grind can get incredibly tedious as you level up.

The multiplayer aspect isn't really good. There's no way to see a list of Join Requests like you can with World and Wilds, so you either have to hope someone is doing a specific quest and happened to send out an SOS, or input very particular parameters if you're queueing for random anomaly quests. You can also search for a random quest, but it's annoying if there's a specific drop you want to farm. The anomaly system does make multiplayer a bit more divided compared to the other games, as you cannot join an anomaly investigation if your AR is even one level below it. In MR, the game gives you support hunters to unlock, which can tag along with you in solo quests. Some of them are very aggressive, while others are more support-oriented. There are lots of them to choose from, so you can experiment a ton with what works.

The base game is incredibly mid. I would honestly only get Rise if you get Sunbreak with it. I see a lot of reviews from people calling the game repetitive with their playtime suggesting they only made it to high rank, and I have to agree. I wish the base game was better, but Sunbreak is well worth it.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that Palamutes handle poorly during movement and combat.

citations.review_text:
Monster Hunter: Rise, I am sorry I was so harsh to you. I never hated you for trying to be different, only for the ways I felt like you compromised the formula. Thank you, Monster Hunter developers, for trying to do new things with the series; for trying to experiment with what ways things could be changed to keep things fresh and fun. I don't think you really found any of it with this game? But I must give you props for trying instead of doing the same exact game over and over and letting the series stagnate into obscurity and burnout. 
HOWEVER I don't think that the short comings should be glossed over and forgotten about. I think that critical analysis is required if you actually care about this series. 

tl;dr Monster Hunter: Rise messes with the formula to create something quicker and more honed in on fighting monsters than previous entries. But in some ways it is more faithful to older games than Monster Hunter: World was. I dislike most of the aesthetics of this game, I think making it primarily for the Switch was a awful move for everyone who wasn't playing on the Switch and I can't even confirm if it's a good experience on there. The switch skills were an excellent idea and I look forward to their return. My opinions on the new monster designs are mixed though, my thorn is Almudron and my rose is definitely Goss Harag.
But the monsters are not what really gets me. What really gets me is how the Palamute is used and general hunter power creep. Though the Palamute can not take you directly to a monster like the Raider Ride in World does, it serves as a vessel for the maps to be bigger and emptier without adding more stuff to them. I'm quite fond of this new kind of companion, but I dislike how it helps to corral you in to breezing over these maps. If you aren't riding the dog around quests, then you're probably launching yourself around with wirebugs. I think wirebugs are tight on a mechanical level but they introduce so much power creep I can not condone the…

I beat the game and it's associated DLC and I gotta say it's really fun. I love the improvements to it over world (Especially performance and Multiplayer support), and there are some really stand out fights to be had in this game. I personally had the most fun with Magnamalo and Mizutsune (my beloved)

The progression makes sense and upgrading your weapons and armor is a pretty easy process once you get the hang of it and have the materials. There's a lot of interesting systems like Argosy, Meowcenaries, the buddy system in general really, research quests, etc... to dive into if you want, or if you don't want. 

Not everything is perfect though. The Palamutes handle like an overweight cruise ship and are equally frustrating to mount during a battle, the controls are unresponsive, unreliable, and floaty, whoever decided to make the radial menu lock your camera deserves to step on 1x1 lego bricks with force every morning for the rest of their life, and despite there being hours of tutorial, it still manages to leave out some incredibly basic information about gameplay. 

I would still reccomend it though, I had a lot of fun. On and just mod Better hunter notes into the game. Just do it, I don't know why the developers decided "alphabetical order" was for neolithic cave dwellers.
